Subject: Ecosystem ops handshake: Datadog + Grafana + Observify — integration checkpoints

Hi Maya / Ellen / Ram —

Thanks for agreeing to explore a coordinated integration path between Datadog, Grafana, Observify and Redwood. At a high level we want to make it easy for customers to: (1) ship OTLP data from Redwood-hosted inference to monitoring backends, (2) have clear SSO/SCIM flows for managed connector installs, and (3) publish a joint troubleshooting runbook for field teams.

Attached is a short project brief that describes scope and success metrics (redwood_project_brief.pdf). Can we book a technical ops sync the week of Nov 8 to align on APIs and required artifacts? Proposed agenda (30–45m):
- Mutual Action Plan review & milestones
- OTLP/exporter config and sample traces/logs
- Auth: SAML/OIDC and service account requirements
- Support/field handoff and runbook owner

If Nov 8–12 works please propose 30–45m slots in your calendars; timezone preference: PT mornings.

Thanks — brief ask is we come out with a draft MAP and an exporter sample by Nov 17.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Partner Integrations, Redwood Inference

Sofia — thanks for the brief and proposed agenda. Nov 9 or Nov 10 morning PT works for our partner eng team; I put a tentative Tues Nov 9 10:00am PT on the calendar (please accept if that works).

Couple quick asks so we can come prepared:
- Can you share a sample OTLP batch (traces + logs) or a short curl that pushes an example payload?
- We'll want to confirm the authorization model: are you planning to support short-lived service tokens, or will customers use OAuth client credentials for Datadog connectors? (I attached a note on OAuth scope we typically request).
- For SSO/SCIM: Ellen from Grafana, can you confirm whether you prefer SAML or OIDC for partner-managed connector provisioning?

I'll attach our high-level connector checklist (datadog_oauth_scope.txt) — happy to walk through it on the call.

Thanks Sofia — glad to be included. From Grafana's side a couple of notes ahead of the sync:
- SSO/Provisioning: we support both SAML and OIDC; for partner-led installs we typically recommend OIDC client credentials + SCIM for user provisioning. We'll need a TLS cert for any webhook endpoints and a public key for JWT verification if you plan to mint tokens.
- Agent compatibility: please include which OTLP exporter versions you will publish and whether you plan to support batching and compression; those details help us advise customers on ingestion limits.
- Observability UX: we'd like to align on default dashboards and a suggested set of alerting rules to ship with the connector.

I can share a short cert checklist on the call.
